items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: I had told Mr. Howard Jacobs that's where this tune was born. He in turn laughed at it.

ctx.x: Yes, it's very clear and it's not rude.

I don't want to be rude. That's where that idea comes. I had told Mr. Howard Jacobs that's where this tune was born. He in turn laughed at it. But I'm telling you the truth of the tune. Where the tunes come in, my inability as a gifted musician, only having a few little ideas about me to put to use the different parts and make a number. I'll tie you on the cuff. I'll tie you on the cuff. I'll tie you on the cuff. Here we go. Howard Jacobs is a man who writes Remmelade. He was sent here by the Newsweek people to…

Now if there's any man living that knows anything about the Mopah Blues, which was played in New Orleans ten years before I went to Chicago, they'll attest to this tune when they hear it. With the exception of the introduction and the runs. The runs were made purposely so whoever on this tune could cry to sound something like the Liverstable Blues. Now we won the suit, we got the royalties from the Liverstable Blues, from the Victor people, and we are next to peace which I'm sorry to say that I didn't want. But…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: He wrote Howard Jacobs and asked him and sent an article in the paper that he would like to reach some old jazz man.

ctx.x: No. It's going now. This is a letter. At the head is Dr. Admiral Sushaw, New Orleans. They, December 29, 1949. Dear Mr. LaRock, resuming our conversation of last night, I would simply write to repeat. The Marcus of Donegal wrote me and asked me to communicate to you. His address is, the Marcus of Donegal, 16 High Park Gate, London, SWF, England. As you know, Lord Donegal is head of all the jazz clubs of Great Britain. They're planning to have a 30-year centennial commemorating the opening up of the original Dixie…

Well, that'll go to show you how a man can speak out of both sides of his mouth. I received a letter. Now, there's been plenty going on after Marshall Steins had given Tom Brown this favorable write-up. Brown was to go to different papers and have this printed and show it as real history. This was lying history connived by this man, Marshall Steins, who somewhere along in the front of these reels, you'll read his letter that he admitted to me he was lying. Now, they come up with more lies. There's a man from…
